turns.prompt_text: I live in Iowa, I am a veteran with an honorable discharge, I would like to apply for a concealed carry (WP5), do I need a permit to purchase a firearm (WP3) as well?
turns.response_html:
No, you do not need a separate permit to purchase a firearm.

Iowa law changed significantly in July 2021 when it became a constitutional carry state. Because of this, the Permit to Acquire (WP3) is entirely optional. Even better, if you choose to get your Nonprofessional Permit to Carry Weapons (WP5), that carry permit completely doubles as your permit to purchase.

First, thank you for your service. Because of your military background, the application process for your carry permit is incredibly straightforward.

How Your Carry Permit (WP5) Replaces the Purchase Permit

When you go to buy a handgun from a Federal Firearms Licensee (FFL) in Iowa, you have two options under current law:

  1. Purchase with a Carry Permit: If you present a valid Iowa Permit to Carry (WP5), you bypass the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) check at the counter. The permit is your background check verification, allowing you to take the firearm home immediately.
  2. Purchase without any permit: You can legally buy a firearm without any permit at all. The dealer will simply run a standard NICS background check right there at the point of sale.

Because a Carry Permit bypasses the background check fee/wait at the counter, most gun owners choose to just get the WP5 rather than maintaining a separate WP3.

The Veteran Advantage for Your Permit to Carry (WP5)

Typically, Iowa requires civilians to take a certified handgun safety course to get a carry permit. However, as a veteran with an honorable discharge, your military small arms training completely waives the civilian training requirement.

Here is exactly what you need to apply at your local county sheriff's office:

  • Your DD-214: You must bring a copy of your DD-214 showing an "Honorable Discharge" or "General Discharge Under Honorable Conditions" (per Iowa Code § 724.9). This serves as your official proof of training.
  • Valid Photo ID: A current Iowa driver's license or state ID card. The address on your ID must match your current residential address in the county where you are applying. (If you've moved recently and your ID isn't updated, bring a hard copy utility bill or lease agreement to prove residency).
  • Application Fee: It is typically $50 for a new 5-year permit. Note: Check your specific county sheriff's website before going, as many Iowa civil offices accept cash only.

Once submitted, the sheriff’s office will process your background check and mail your 5-year uniform permit card to your home address, usually within a few weeks.
